sets.title: Set 1: Original Exam Questions
sets.description: The original MCQs from the September 2019 class Block 3 Supplementary College Final Exam paper (Kenya Registered Nursing, sat 6 December 2022, Multiple Choice Questions, Q81 to Q100).

questions.text: Recommended time to commence enteral feeding in a child who had undergone pyloromyotomy is:

options.B: As soon as the patient wakes up
options.D: As soon as the patient’s appetite returns.

questions.explanation: As soon as the patient wakes up (B) is correct as the best answer because after a pyloromyotomy (splitting of the thickened pyloric muscle in pyloric stenosis) the bowel itself has not been opened, so there is no need to wait for bowel sounds, and current practice is to start feeds early, within about 4 to 6 hours once the baby is awake and recovered from the anaesthetic, with small, frequent breast or formula feeds that are increased to full feeds, because early feeding shortens the hospital stay. Immediate post-operative period (A) is incorrect because the baby is still drowsy from the anaesthetic and could aspirate. When bowel sounds return (C) is incorrect as the best answer because it is the rule after bowel surgery with an anastomosis, and is not needed after pyloromyotomy, although some older texts use it. As soon as the patient's appetite returns (D) is incorrect because a baby cannot report appetite, and waiting for it delays feeding and hydration. Note: older nursing texts accept option C, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: Total volume of fluids to infuse in the first 8 hours for a child who sustained 25% burn surface area and is weighing 14kg is:
questions.explanation: 700mls (B) is correct because by the Parkland formula the total fluid for the first 24 hours is 4 ml x body weight (kg) x percentage of burned surface area = 4 x 14 x 25 = 1400 ml, and half of this volume (1400 divided by 2 = 700 ml) is given in the first 8 hours from the time of the burn, and the other half in the next 16 hours. 280 ml (A) is incorrect because it comes from using a wrong factor (about 0.8 ml per kg per percent). 840 ml (C) is incorrect because it is 60 percent of the 24-hour volume and is not the Parkland share. 1400 ml (D) is incorrect because it is the whole 24-hour volume. Note: in young children, maintenance fluid is added to the Parkland volume in some protocols, but the question gives only the Parkland data.

questions.text: Baby A, 2 months old has tested positive for HIV antibodies. Baby A will be classified as:
questions.explanation: HIV exposed (B) is correct because the mother's HIV antibodies cross the placenta and stay in the baby's blood until 18 months of age, so an antibody (rapid) test that is positive in a child under 18 months only shows that the baby has been exposed to HIV, and does not show infection; the infection is confirmed by a DNA PCR (virological) test, and the baby is given cotrimoxazole prophylaxis and followed up. Confirmed HIV infection (A) is incorrect because it needs a positive PCR result. Suspected HIV infection (C) is incorrect because this IMNCI category applies to a child with a positive antibody test, with signs of illness. Symptomatic HIV infection (D) is incorrect because the baby has no clinical signs mentioned, and symptomatic infection is a clinical classification.

questions.text: According to IMNCI a child with the following signs will require URGENT referral:
questions.explanation: Vomiting everything, fever (A) is correct because vomiting everything is one of the general danger signs in IMNCI (with inability to drink or breastfeed, convulsions, and lethargy or unconsciousness), and a child with any danger sign is classified as having a very severe disease, given pre-referral treatment and referred urgently. Cough, symptomatic HIV infection (B) is incorrect because it is not by itself an urgent referral and it is managed according to the severity of the cough and the HIV care plan. Anaemia, fever (C) is incorrect because only severe anaemia (severe palmar pallor) or very severe febrile disease with danger signs needs urgent referral. Sunken eyes, restlessness (D) is incorrect because they are signs of some dehydration, which is treated with ORS (Plan B) and does not need urgent referral, unlike severe dehydration (lethargy, unable to drink).

questions.text: During history taking, Mr. Zee is observed to be giving irrelevant details and digressions before giving the correct response. This is referred to as:
questions.explanation: Circumstantiality (D) is correct because the patient gives unnecessary detail and goes off the point (digressions), but in the end comes back to the question and gives the answer. Tangentiality (A) is incorrect because the speech wanders off the subject and never returns to answer the question. Verbigeration (B) is incorrect because it is the meaningless, stereotyped repetition of words or phrases. Neologisms (C) is incorrect because they are newly invented words with a meaning known only to the patient.

questions.text: Typical antipsychotics cause extrapyramidal side – effects because of their effect on:
questions.explanation: D2 receptors (B) is correct because typical antipsychotics (for example haloperidol and chlorpromazine) strongly block the D2 dopamine receptors in the mesolimbic pathway, which controls psychotic symptoms, and also in the nigrostriatal pathway, which controls movement, so the loss of dopamine action there causes extrapyramidal side effects (dystonia, parkinsonism, akathisia and tardive dyskinesia). D1 (A), D3 (C) and D4 (D) receptors are incorrect because the extrapyramidal effects of the typical drugs are linked mainly to D2 blockade, and not to these receptors.

questions.text: An appropriate nursing intervention for a client in a manic episode who comes for a group therapy session dressed in a provocative and physically revealing outfit is to:

options.A: Do nothing and allow her to learn from the responses of her peers
options.B: Tell the client she cannot wear this outfit while she is in the hospital
options.C: Explain to her that if she wears this outfit she must remain in her room
options.D: Quietly walk with her back to her room and help her change clothes

questions.explanation: Quietly walk with her back to her room and help her change clothes (D) is correct because the manic patient has poor judgement and no insight, so the nurse protects her dignity and privacy, avoids embarrassing her in front of the group, and gives calm, non-judgemental help, which keeps her safe from ridicule and allows her to join the group appropriately dressed. Do nothing and allow her to learn from the responses of her peers (A) is incorrect because it leaves the patient exposed to humiliation and the group disrupted. Tell the client she cannot wear this outfit while she is in the hospital (B) is incorrect because it is a confrontational statement that can provoke anger and does not help. Explain to her that if she wears this outfit she must remain in her room (C) is incorrect because it is a threat of punishment, and is not therapeutic.

questions.text: To aid in retrieval of memory for patients with dissociative amnesia, the patient should be:
questions.explanation: Given sodium amobarbital (B) is correct because in dissociative amnesia the memory loss is caused by psychological trauma and not by brain damage, and an intravenous sedative-hypnotic such as sodium amobarbital (an amobarbital interview, sometimes called a 'truth serum') relaxes the patient and lowers the psychological defences so that the repressed memories can be retrieved; hypnosis is another method. Diazepam (A) is incorrect because it is an anxiolytic that sedates the patient and can itself impair memory. Electroconvulsive therapy (C) is incorrect because it is used in severe depression and catatonia, and it causes memory loss. Systematic desensitization (D) is incorrect because it is a behavioural technique for phobias and anxiety, using graded exposure to the feared object.

questions.text: The process of psychoanalysis and hypnosis in which a patient is guided to mentally re – experience the past traumatic events is referred to as:
questions.explanation: Abreaction (B) is correct because it is the release of emotion by re-living (mentally re-experiencing) a past traumatic event, in psychoanalysis or under hypnosis or sedation, so that the buried feelings are expressed and relieved. Hypnosis (A) is incorrect because it is the trance-like state of focused attention that may be used to bring about abreaction, not the re-experiencing itself. Transference (C) is incorrect because it is the unconscious shifting of the patient's feelings about an important person from the past onto the therapist. Countertransference (D) is incorrect because it is the therapist's unconscious emotional reaction to the patient.

questions.text: A sampling frame is essential in:
questions.explanation: Systematic random sampling (B) is correct because a sampling frame (the complete list of all members of the population) is needed to calculate the sampling interval (population size divided by sample size), to choose a random starting point and to pick every kth unit; it is needed in all probability sampling methods (simple random, stratified, systematic). Snowballing (A) is incorrect because participants are found by referral from earlier participants, with no list. Quota sampling (C) is incorrect because the units are picked non-randomly to fill set quotas of the characteristics, with no list. Purposive sampling (D) is incorrect because the researcher deliberately selects the participants who are best suited to the study.

questions.text: A feature of qualitative research is:

options.C: Uses controlled setting to collect data
options.D: The analytical techniques are predominantly deductive

questions.explanation: Themes are generated during analysis (B) is correct because qualitative research collects words, observations and stories, and the analysis is inductive: the researcher codes the data and groups the codes into themes that emerge from the data. Data obtained is purely numerical (A) is incorrect because numerical data is a feature of quantitative research. Uses controlled setting to collect data (C) is incorrect because controlled settings (such as experiments) belong to quantitative research, while qualitative studies are done in natural settings. The analytical techniques are predominantly deductive (D) is incorrect because deductive analysis (testing a hypothesis) is typical of quantitative research.

questions.text: An example of a probability sampling method is:
questions.explanation: Cluster (C) is correct because in cluster sampling the population is divided into groups (clusters, such as villages or wards) and some clusters are chosen at random, so every unit has a known chance of selection, which makes it a probability method (the others are simple random, stratified and systematic sampling). Quota (A), accidental (B) and snowballing (D) are incorrect because they are non-probability methods, in which the chance of selection is unknown, and the participants are chosen by convenience, availability or referral.

questions.text: A nurse is conducting a research on use of the CAUTI bundle for one month by reviewing patient records in the ward. The research design used is:
questions.explanation: Cross-sectional (D) is correct as the best answer because the data is collected over one short, fixed period (one month) at a single point in time, without following the same patients over time, which is the defining feature of a cross-sectional (descriptive) design. Prospective (A) is incorrect because it follows the participants forward in time from the exposure to an outcome that has not yet happened. Retrospective (B) is incorrect as the best answer because it looks back at events that have already happened, and although the data come from records, the question emphasises the one-month period of the study. Longitudinal (C) is incorrect because it follows the same subjects repeatedly over a long period. Note: a review of existing records can also be called retrospective, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: Variables that can be measured on the ratio scale include:
questions.explanation: Weight, Height (D) is correct because the ratio scale has equal intervals and a true (absolute) zero, so ratios are meaningful (20 kg is twice 10 kg), and both weight and height fit this. Gender and blood pressure (A) is incorrect because gender is a nominal variable (blood pressure is ratio, but the pair is not). Marital status and temperature (B) is incorrect because marital status is nominal and temperature in degrees Celsius is on the interval scale, with no true zero. Pulse and race (C) is incorrect because race is a nominal variable.

questions.text: Dexamethasone is administered to a mother with premature rupture of the membranes before 34 weeks of gestation in order to:
questions.explanation: Enable fetal lung maturity (C) is correct because antenatal corticosteroids (dexamethasone or betamethasone) cross the placenta and stimulate the fetal lungs to produce surfactant, which reduces the risk of respiratory distress syndrome, intraventricular haemorrhage and death in a baby likely to be born before 34 weeks. Prevent inflammation (A) is incorrect because the aim is not an anti-inflammatory effect, and infection is prevented by antibiotics. Reduce pain (B) is incorrect because dexamethasone is not an analgesic. Prevent oligohydramnios (D) is incorrect because the low liquor follows the rupture of the membranes and cannot be prevented by steroids.

questions.text: Kegel exercises are performed after delivery in order to:

options.A: Strengthen pelvic floor muscles and prevent urinary incontinence
options.B: Promote voiding and healing of the episiotomy site
options.C: Relieve pain during voiding, prevent urinary incontinence
options.D: Tighten abdominal muscles and promote perineal healing

questions.explanation: Strengthen pelvic floor muscles and prevent urinary incontinence (A) is correct because Kegel exercises (repeated contraction and relaxation of the pubococcygeus muscles, as if stopping the flow of urine) restore the tone of the pelvic floor, which is stretched by pregnancy and delivery, and so prevent stress urinary incontinence and uterine prolapse, and also improve circulation to the perineum. Promote voiding and healing of the episiotomy site (B) is incorrect because voiding is promoted by fluids and ambulation, and the exercises are not aimed at voiding. Relieve pain during voiding, prevent urinary incontinence (C) is incorrect because the exercises do not treat pain. Tighten abdominal muscles and promote perineal healing (D) is incorrect because the abdominal muscles are exercised with other postnatal exercises such as pelvic tilting.

questions.text: Risk factors to placenta abruption include:
questions.explanation: Impacting accident, Hypertension (B) is correct because abdominal trauma (road accident, fall, domestic violence) can shear the placenta off the uterine wall, and hypertension (chronic, or pre-eclampsia) is the commonest risk factor, since it damages the blood vessels of the decidua; other risk factors are multiparity, previous abruption, smoking, cocaine use, sudden decompression of the uterus and a short cord. Placenta praevia, multiparous (A) is incorrect because placenta praevia is a separate cause of antepartum haemorrhage, even though multiparity is a risk. Short cord, placenta abruption (C) is incorrect because the abruption itself cannot be its own risk factor. Hypertension, anaemia (D) is incorrect because anaemia is not an established risk factor for abruption.

questions.text: In fetal circulation, the blood vessel from the umbilical vein to the inferior vena cava which carries oxygenated blood to the heart is:
questions.explanation: Ductus venosus (A) is correct because it is the fetal shunt that connects the umbilical vein to the inferior vena cava, so that most of the oxygenated blood from the placenta bypasses the liver and goes to the right atrium; after birth it closes and becomes the ligamentum venosum. Foramen ovale (B) is incorrect because it is the opening between the right and left atria. Ductus arteriosus (C) is incorrect because it connects the pulmonary artery to the aorta, so that blood bypasses the lungs. Hypogastric arteries (D) is incorrect because they are the internal iliac arteries, which become the umbilical arteries and carry deoxygenated blood to the placenta.

questions.text: A client received a Depo-Provera injection two months ago, she comes to the MCH clinic because she has missed her period. The appropriate intervention is:

options.B: Reassure her she is not pregnant
options.D: Advise her to return to the clinic if amenorrhea continues

questions.explanation: Reassure her she is not pregnant (B) is correct as the best answer because Depo-Provera (DMPA) is given every 3 months and protects against pregnancy for 13 weeks, so a client who was injected 2 months ago is still protected, and amenorrhoea (or irregular bleeding) is a very common and harmless effect of the progestin, which thins the lining of the uterus, so the nurse counsels and reassures her. Checking for pregnancy (A) is incorrect as the best answer because it is only needed if she is overdue for her injection or has signs of pregnancy, although it is a reasonable step. Refer her for prenatal counseling (C) is incorrect because there is no evidence of pregnancy. Advise her to return to the clinic if amenorrhea continues (D) is incorrect because amenorrhoea is expected to continue while she is on the method, and it is not a reason to return. Note: option A is defensible, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: When preparing a mother who is 2 days postpartum for discharge, the nurse recommends the following contraceptive methods to be avoided during exclusive breastfeeding:
questions.explanation: Combined oral contraceptive (D) is correct because the oestrogen in the combined pill reduces the quantity of breast milk, and it can pass to the baby in the milk, so it is avoided in the first 6 months of exclusive breastfeeding (and until the baby is 6 weeks old at least, as per the eligibility criteria), and it also raises the risk of blood clots in the early postpartum period. Female condom (A) is incorrect because it is a barrier method with no hormones, and is safe. Progestin only pills (B) are incorrect because they do not affect milk supply, and are suitable for breastfeeding mothers. Hormone releasing intrauterine device (C) is incorrect because the levonorgestrel IUD acts locally, and is safe in breastfeeding women once inserted after the recommended time.
